title: A three tier rapid mass programming method
author: Steane, Trifilo, et al.

steps.title: Assemble tower hardware
steps.instruction: Build each tower module by connecting a Raspberry Pi (Local Controller) to the custom PCB that holds up to 15 ESP‑01 target devices; plug the Pi into the network via Ethernet (or a switch), attach the power supply that provides 5 V to the Pi and 3.3 V to each ESP, and insert the ESP modules into the PCB sockets in any X, Y, Z orientation (90° daughter boards can be used). The PCB uses two 1:8 analog multiplexers and an enable line to route the four ESP pins (Tx, Rx, Chip_enable, RST) through four data GPIO pins and four select GPIO pins (total 8 GPIO) on the Pi, allowing bi‑directional serial communication without pre‑configuration.

substeps.instruction: Connect Raspberry Pi Ethernet port to the Master PC network.
Supply 5 V to the Pi and 3.3 V to all ESP pins via the tower power circuitry.
Insert up to 15 ESP‑01 modules into the PCB sockets, arranging orientation as needed.
Ensure the multiplexing circuit (2 × 1:8 Mux devices + enable line) is wired to the Pi’s 8 GPIO pins (4 data, 4 select).

steps.title: Prepare firmware image files
steps.instruction: Compile or obtain the binary image files that will be flashed onto the ESP‑01 target devices; each file should be ready for direct programming with ESPtool.

steps.title: Create YAML configuration file
steps.instruction: Write a YAML‑formatted configuration file that lists the image file aliases at the top, then defines each tower and the specific target devices (by socket number) that should receive each image; only devices listed will be programmed.

steps.title: Start Master Controller
steps.instruction: Run the Master Controller Python script on the PC; the script opens a TCP socket, uses multithreading to accept connections, and creates a new thread for each Local Controller (tower) that connects.

steps.title: Start Local Controllers
steps.instruction: On each Raspberry Pi, launch the Local Controller Python script; on start‑up it automatically attempts to connect to the Master Controller via its Ethernet port and prepares ESPtool for flashing.

steps.title: Transfer image files to towers
steps.instruction: For each image file, the Master Controller sends the filename and file size to the appropriate Local Controller for validation, then streams the file data over the TCP connection.

steps.title: Send programming commands
steps.instruction: After all files are transferred, the Master Controller reads the YAML configuration and issues programming commands to each Local Controller, specifying which image to flash to which target device.

steps.title: Flash and restart target device
steps.instruction: Each Local Controller selects the target ESP by setting the four select GPIO pins on the multiplexers, then uses ESPtool over the two serial pins (Tx/Rx) and two control pins (Chip_enable, RST) to flash the assigned image; once flashing completes, the device is automatically restarted.

steps.title: Log programming results
steps.instruction: The Local Controller records the success or failure of each flash and sends the status back to the Master Controller, which logs the results for all devices.
